content: Versioned terms re-acceptance: strongest legal posture is clickwrap - explicit checkbox at signup, and for existing users an in-app blocking acknowledgement before continued access. Consent record must store user id, timestamp, IP address and the exact terms VERSION accepted; each version stored separately and immutably archived so acceptance links to the text as it stood. Courts enforce clickwrap when terms are conspicuous and acceptance unmistakable; passive 'continued use = acceptance' is legally weaker. Best practice is to re-prompt or give ~30 days notice on material changes. Implication: a single 'termos.atualizadoEm' timestamp is insufficient - need an immutable version row plus a per-user acceptance row.
